question: What is the main purpose of a desktop environment in an operating system?

options.A: It repairs corrupted hardware components automatically inside the system unit
options.B: It generates physical electricity to power the computer monitor and keyboard
options.C: It permanently translates word documents into different international languages
options.D: It provides a visual graphical user interface for interacting with the computer

explanation: The desktop environment turns computer processes into an easy-to-use visual screen with icons, windows, and pointers. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do operating systems use a desktop layout instead of text commands?

options.A: To make computer navigation more intuitive and accessible for everyday users
options.B: To increase the processing speed of the central processing unit drastically
options.C: To reduce the amount of physical storage space needed on the hard drive
options.D: To eliminate the need for an operating system altogether during startup

explanation: Visual desktops use familiar office concepts so users do not need to memorize complex text commands. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h1)

question: What does the acronym WIMP stand for in computer systems?
explanation: WIMP stands for Windows, Icons, Menus, and Pointers, which make up the standard screen layout for graphical interfaces. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which part of the WIMP system shows a running app in a frame on the screen?
explanation: Windows are the bordered areas on the screen that hold active programs or open documents. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is another common name for a file directory?
explanation: Computer directories are called folders, much like physical office filing systems. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h3)

question: How does a folder tree help organize computer files?

options.A: By converting all text files into secure formats that cannot be edited
options.B: By compressing file sizes automatically to save valuable storage capacity
options.C: By grouping related documents into nested folders to prevent clutter and loss
options.D: By deleting duplicate files across the hard drive without user approval

explanation: Folder structures let you place subfolders inside main folders to keep files neatly organized. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which type of file path shows the complete address starting from the root directory?
explanation: An absolute path gives the full, exact route to a file starting from the top level of the drive. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h4)

question: If you are already working inside a folder named 'Practicals', how can you most easily open a file inside that same folder?
explanation: When working inside a folder, a relative path lets you open a file simply by using its name. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is it unhelpful to name important files with vague titles like 'Document1'?

options.A: It makes finding the specific content difficult later when searching through storage
options.B: It prevents the file from being opened by any word processing application
options.C: It increases the physical file size beyond normal hard drive limits
options.D: It causes the computer operating system to crash during routine updates

explanation: Clear file names let you know what is inside a document right away without opening it. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT recommended when organizing digital files?

options.A: Using clear and descriptive folder titles for different academic subjects
options.B: Creating subfolders to categorize documents by date or topic
options.C: Backing up important study notes to a secure cloud storage account
options.D: Storing all academic and personal documents directly on the main desktop screen

explanation: Cluttering the desktop makes files hard to find and slows down the computer; files belong in organized folders. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T2#BMP123_U2_T2_h5)
